topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.

papers.title: Automation in sleep state classification and maturity evaluation of EEG in preterm-born infants.
papers.abstract: There is a growing need to automate EEG monitoring of preterm-born infants, particularly where expert evaluation is limited. However, existing models necessitate human intervention for comprehensive assessment, thereby limiting the clinical applicability. We collected 165 EEG records from 65 preterm-born infants. 8-channel EEG records were segmented every 30second and allocated into eight classes (three preterm-equivalent, four term-equivalent, and one noise class). We performed noise detection, sleep state classification, and maturity assessment through the classification. ImageNet pretrained ResNet-50 was finetuned to classify the segmented EEG images. A novel index, named "maturity rate," was calculated as the proportion of term-equivalent labels in each EEG recording. The model achieved a macro F1 score of 0.58 and Cohen's Kappa of 0.58 for the 8-class classification. When the labels were merged into active sleep, quiet sleep, and noise categories, performance improved to an F1 score of 0.84 and Kappa of 0.74. The maturity rate increased continuously with postmenstrual age at the time of recording, reflecting functional brain development beyond the term-preterm dichotomy. Our model enables end-to-end EEG assessment of sleeping newborns by simultaneously performing noise detection, sleep state classification, and maturity assessment, with minimal need for human intervention.

papers.title: A hidden Markov model for unsupervised EEG-based tracking of auditory attention to a single voice
papers.abstract: Objective: Absolute auditory attention decoding (aAAD) aims to track how strongly a listener attends to a single speech source using electroencephalography (EEG). Unlike selective auditory attention decoding, aAAD lacks a competing speech reference, making reliable attention tracking challenging. Approach: We propose a fully unsupervised aAAD pipeline combining neural envelope tracking (NET) with hidden Markov model (HMM)-based temporal inference. Using EEG signals and the target speech envelope, the framework estimates a continuous attention trajectory without explicit attention-state labels. We evaluate the approach using EEG recordings from 30 adults, investigate the impact of analysis window length, and compare HMM post-processing with moving-average (MA) smoothing and alternative EEG features. Main results: With 1-s analysis windows, non-causal HMM post-processing improves the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for all 30 participants, increasing mean AUC from 0.547 for raw NET to 0.832. A 5-s window achieves the highest mean AUC of 0.858. Compared with non-causal MA smoothing, the HMM achieves higher AUC across the examined smoothing scales. Individual switch detection times are comparable, while the HMM generally achieves lower group-level detection times. NET also outperforms alpha power and spectral entropy as an observation feature in the unsupervised HMM framework. Significance: The proposed framework provides a label-free approach for estimating temporal fluctuations in auditory attention, demonstrating the utility of probabilistic temporal inference for continuous attention tracking in single-speaker listening scenarios.

ai.reason: Fully unsupervised HMM-based temporal inference on EEG attention trajectories directly transfers to sleep/vigilance staging without labels, with practical window-length analysis and CPU-friendly post-processing.
ai.summary: We propose a fully unsupervised aAAD pipeline combining neural envelope tracking (NET) with hidden Markov model (HMM)-based temporal inference to track auditory attention to a single voice from EEG. With 1-s windows, HMM post-processing increased mean AUC from 0.547 for raw NET to 0.832 across 30 participants, and a 5-s window achieved the highest mean AUC of 0.858.

papers.title: Real-time noise cancellation for EEG monitoring and brain-computer interfaces
papers.abstract: Raw electroencephalography (EEG) data suffer from a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Effective real-time cleaning of EEG would improve the robustness of EEG monitoring, brain-computer interfaces, and brain-state-dependent stimulation applications in both laboratory and real-life environments. Here, we present a real-time source-estimate-utilizing noise-discarding algorithm (rtSOUND) for EEG noise suppression. We adapted the established offline SOUND algorithm for real-time use and implemented it into an open-source EEG-processing software. Instead of using conventional temporal filtering, SOUND operates the data with a spatial filter. This makes it particularly suitable for real-time applications, since each streamed data sample can be cleaned separately in near real-time. Unlike temporal filtering methods, SOUND does not make assumptions about the frequency content of noise and brain signals but assumes that the noise topographies differ from those generated by brain activity. With an EEG forward model, rtSOUND cross-validates the EEG time series and estimates the spatial distribution of noise, resulting in a data-cleaning linear spatial filter. Each streamed EEG sample is processed synchronously, and the filter is periodically updated in an asynchronous parallel process. The algorithm rapidly updates the spatial filter in response to changes in the data, ensuring that noise reduction is both immediate and accurately adapted to the current EEG state. rtSOUND was validated with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-EEG and resting-state EEG datasets measured from 25 healthy subjects. SNR of both TMS-evoked potentials and resting-state data consistently improved across various metrics. rtSOUND particularly benefitted channels with poor SNR, while retaining the waveforms in high-quality channels. The algorithm was fast enough to process data streamed at 5 kHz. rtSOUND improves the SNR of EEG in real time, providing a robust method to improve signal quality for brain-state-monitoring applications.

ai.reason: Open-source, real-time spatial-filter noise cancellation makes no frequency assumptions and is readily adaptable across recording systems and animals, matching the artifact-removal and GUI-integration priorities.
ai.summary: We present rtSOUND, a real-time source-estimate-utilizing noise-discarding algorithm for EEG noise suppression that uses a spatial filter updated asynchronously to clean each streamed sample. Validated on TMS-EEG and resting-state data from 25 healthy subjects, rtSOUND consistently improved SNR across metrics, particularly for low-SNR channels, while retaining waveforms in high-quality channels and processing data at 5 kHz.

papers.title: Cross-cohort transfer of clinical Alzheimer's EEG signatures to cognitively healthy APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 risk carriers using differentiable logic gate networks.
papers.abstract: Neural alterations associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) may emerge years before clinical diagnosis, and genetic risk factors such as APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 may identify individuals vulnerable to these shifts. We tested whether electroencephalography (EEG) signatures learned from clinically diagnosed AD patients transfer to cognitively healthy middle-aged adults carrying these variants. Differentiable logic gate networks (Diff-Logic) and neural baselines were trained on log-relative power spectral density features from a clinical cohort of AD patients and cognitively normal (CN) controls. These models were then applied without retraining to an independent genetic-risk cohort of neutral-risk non-carriers (N), APOE-ε4-only carriers (A+P-), and dual APOE-ε4/PICALM G-allele carriers (A+P+), yielding a continuous AD-like EEG signature score per participant. Diff-Logic matched neural baselines in clinical classification (balanced accuracy 0.809±0.028; AUROC 0.845±0.023) while enabling edge inference with a 7.4× model-size reduction and 0.22 ms model-only latency on a 7 W single-core CPU. In the genetic-risk cohort, scores were highest in A+P+ participants (0.393±0.167) relative to N (0.296±0.154) and A+P- (0.285±0.143; subject-level mean ± SD). This elevation was nominally significant before correction (A+P+ vs. A+P-, punc=0.036) but did not survive Holm correction (pHolm=0.109), and the cohort carried no AD pathology or conversion ground truth; the association was therefore exploratory. Integrated gradients attribution of the trained model showed genetic-risk relevance in delta, theta, and alpha, partially overlapping clinical AD topography. These findings support the feasibility of zero-shot EEG transfer in genetically at-risk individuals and highlight the need for replication in larger cohorts. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/Shyamal-Dharia/ad-difflogic-transfer.

ai.reason: Demonstrates transfer learning across cohorts using spectral features, with an efficient differentiable logic gate network that is CPU-friendly and interpretable—highly relevant for EEG analysis.
ai.summary: Tested cross-cohort transfer of EEG signatures from clinically diagnosed Alzheimer's disease patients to cognitively healthy APOE-ε4 and PICALM risk carriers using differentiable logic gate networks. The model matched neural baselines in clinical classification (balanced accuracy 0.809) and produced higher AD-like EEG signature scores in dual-risk carriers, though the difference was not significant after correction and remains exploratory.

papers.title: Quantifying Subject-Identity Variance in Spectral EEG Features and Its Role in Machine Learning Evaluation Leakage.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to study cognitive states and clinical biomarkers, yet the contribution of stable between-subject differences to common EEG feature representations is rarely quantified directly or incorporated into evaluation design. Here, we examine subject-linked structure in spectral EEG features using a longitudinal four-session dataset spanning 199 days and replicate key findings across four public datasets covering 39 to 395 participants, multiple paradigms, and recording systems ranging from low-channel consumer devices to research-grade EEG. In spectral band-power representations, subject identity accounted for substantially more variance than session-related drift and supported extremely strong individual discriminability under subject-wise held-out protocols, with high verification performance and robust cross-session recognition over months. However, this identity structure was not fully invariant across paradigms, showing stronger transfer in richer, higher-channel recordings than in low-channel consumer EEG under larger task shifts. We further show that the same subject-linked structure can inflate downstream clinical classification when evaluation is performed with naive segment-level splits, demonstrating that apparent diagnostic performance can partly reflect identity leakage rather than biomarker learning. These findings highlight subject identity as a measurable and persistent source of structured variance in spectral EEG features and support routine use of subject-wise evaluation and explicit confound diagnostics in EEG machine-learning studies.

ai.topic: Subject identity variance in EEG spectral features
ai.reason: Addresses spectral EEG features, subject variability, and evaluation leakage—critical for signal normalization and robust machine learning across datasets and animals.
ai.summary: Quantified subject-identity variance in spectral EEG features using a longitudinal dataset and four public datasets, showing that subject identity accounts for substantial variance and can inflate downstream clinical classification when evaluation uses naive segment-level splits. The findings support subject-wise evaluation and confound diagnostics in EEG machine-learning studies.

papers.title: Gradient-Free Filter Importance for Structured Pruning of Compact EEG Networks.
papers.abstract: Deploying EEG classification networks on resource-constrained brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware motivates structured filter pruning, yet which importance criterion to trust in already-compact architectures is unclear. We present a leakage-free, physically materialized comparison of five filter-importance criteria-ablation-based structural sensitivity analysis (SSA), first-order Taylor, L1-norm, geometric median, and random-across four datasets, two paradigms (motor imagery and ERP), two architectures, multiple capacities, and with and without fine-tuning. On EEGNet, after fine-tuning, SSA and Taylor are statistically equivalent: pooled over the four datasets their accuracy difference falls within a ±1 percentage-point margin (TOST, p=0.01), and on ShallowConvNet SSA is never worse than Taylor; both criteria significantly outperform the weight-based and random ones. SSA's value is therefore not a more accurate ranking but its formulation: on a weight-quantized (8-bit) EEGNet, where the loss gradient-and hence Taylor-is undefined on the quantized graph used here, SSA is the best gradient-free criterion, significantly beating L1, geometric-median, and random pruning in aggregate-extending structured pruning to the quantized, gradient-free but editable deployment regime. We further show that the pruning schedule and fine-tuning matter more than the choice between strong criteria, and that training large then pruning with fine-tuning recovers accuracy equivalent to a directly trained smaller model. The results clarify where the importance criterion does and does not matter for compact EEG decoders.

ai.topic: Gradient-free filter pruning for EEG networks
ai.reason: Addresses structured pruning for compact EEG networks, enabling efficient deployment; directly relevant to CPU-friendly algorithms and open-source analysis software.
ai.summary: Compared five filter-importance criteria for structured pruning of compact EEG networks across four datasets, two paradigms, and two architectures. Found that after fine-tuning, ablation-based SSA and first-order Taylor are statistically equivalent on EEGNet, but SSA is the best gradient-free criterion for quantized (8-bit) EEGNet where gradients are undefined, and pruning schedule and fine-tuning matter more than criterion choice.

papers.title: Scalp EEG and Intrinsic Optical Signal Imaging for Noninvasive Detection of Spreading Depolarizations in the Rat Cortex.
papers.abstract: Spreading depolarization (SD) is a slowly propagating wave of massive neuronal and glial depolarization in the cerebral cortex that occurs in various brain diseases. However, noninvasive SD detection remains challenging. Here, we used scalp EEG and intrinsic optical signal (IOS) recordings in rats of both sexes to assess the feasibility of noninvasively detecting high-potassium-induced SDs in the cortex. Scalp EEG failed to detect DC-shifts but revealed a characteristic SD-related depression of AC-EEG activity, while concurrent infrared IOS recordings captured reliable SD-associated signals. Although the magnitudes of AC-EEG depression and IOS signals during scalp recordings were several times smaller than those recorded epidurally, both techniques enabled high-fidelity SD detection. These findings demonstrate that noninvasive monitoring of scalp EEG and infrared IOS imaging reliably detects SDs in the rat cerebral cortex.

papers.title: Between patterns and predictions: Interpretable latent EEG representations for clinical insights.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures rich brain dynamics, yet in clinical practice this complexity is often reduced to simplified summaries or categorical labels, limiting its interpretability for decision-making. We tested the hypothesis that a pretrained latent embedding framework, the Universal Map of EEG (UM-EEG), can preserve clinically meaningful structure across heterogeneous datasets and provide a generalizable representation of brain states. We applied UM-EEG, without retraining, to three independent cohorts spanning distinct clinical contexts: long-term EEG recordings from cardiac arrest patients (n = 575), subarachnoid hemorrhage (n = 100), and routine clinical EEG recordings containing physiological and pathological patterns (n = 141). EEG segments were projected into a 128-dimensional space anchored by expert-derived reference states, including wakefulness, sleep stages, ictal-interictal continuum activity, and burst suppression. Across datasets, favorable outcome or physiological recordings were consistently located closer to healthy reference states, whereas poor outcome and pathological recordings shifted toward pathological regions of the embedding space. Trajectory-derived geometric and temporal features discriminated outcome in cardiac arrest (ROC-AUC 0.83) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (ROC-AUC 0.76), and distinguished physiological from pathological routine EEGs (ROC-AUC 0.93). In routine EEG, similarity relationships derived from embedding trajectories correlated with those derived from structured clinical reports, indicating that the latent space recapitulates clinically relevant organization. These findings show that a fixed, semantically structured EEG embedding generalizes across etiologies and recording settings, enabling prognostic stratification and contextual interpretation while preserving the relational structure of brain states.

ai.summary: Applied a pretrained Universal Map of EEG latent embedding, without retraining, to three independent clinical cohorts (cardiac arrest n=575, subarachnoid hemorrhage n=100, routine EEG n=141). Trajectory-derived geometric and temporal features discriminated outcome in cardiac arrest (ROC-AUC 0.83) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (ROC-AUC 0.76) and distinguished physiological from pathological routine EEGs (ROC-AUC 0.93).

papers.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.abstract: Deep learning models for electroencephalography (EEG) pathology detection achieve competitive accuracy but offer limited interpretability. In this paper, we introduce concept bottleneck models (CBMs) for EEG pathology detection which use clinical EEG biomarkers computed analytically from the signal as a bottleneck to be used for prediction. Those concepts include band power, spectral ratios, alpha peak frequency and amplitude, hemispheric asymmetry and phase locking values. With the backbone based on shallow convolutional neural network (CNN), we compare a black box baseline with two variants of CBMs. The hybrid variant is a classifier receives a residual projection of the backbone features. The pure variant is a CBM where the classifier receives only the predicted concepts. Models are evaluated on abnormality detection and dementia classification followed by concept prediction quality and leakage analysis. Both CBMs approach the baseline on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) and are 2-5 percentage points lower on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%). The pure CBM exhibits concept fidelity concern where the predicted concepts deviate from their ground truth values. Replacing them with their true values causes severe cost on accuracy by 26 and 22 points on TUAB and CAUEEG. The concept fidelity concern is mitigated by increasing the weight of the concept loss to match the ground truth concepts. the mitigation comes with small accuracy cost on TUAB but a relatively larger cost on CAUEEG. The code of the experiments and full logs are available at https://www.github.com/mhmdrdwn/cbm.

ai.reason: Uses clinically interpretable spectral concepts and shallow CNNs for EEG classification, aligning with interpretable feature extraction and lightweight model priorities.
ai.summary: This study introduces concept bottleneck models for EEG pathology detection that use analytically computed clinical EEG biomarkers (e.g., band power, spectral ratios, phase locking values) as an interpretable bottleneck. The models approach black-box baseline accuracy on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) but show lower performance on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%), with a pure CBM variant exhibiting concept fidelity concerns mitigated by increasing concept loss weight.

papers.title: TSMCA-Net: A Multi-Granular Cross-Attention Framework for Cross-Session EEG-fNIRS Decoding.
papers.abstract: We propose TSMCA-Net, a lightweight cross-session EEG-fNIRS decoder that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with <1M parameters-70.6% fewer than the strongest baseline-while maintaining sub-8ms inference latency. TSMCA-Net decomposes multimodal interactions into three complementary views-temporal-spatial (TS), temporal-modal (TM), and spatial-modal (SM)-through structured multi-view factorization that separates heterogeneous dependency axes while preserving cross-branch information sharing. A Dynamic Multi-Scale Context module adaptively aggregates spatial dependencies on a unified scalp topology, while a causal lag modeling strategy captures delayed hemodynamic responses under strict temporal causality. An asymmetric cross-attention mechanism then integrates the multi-granular representations for role-aware fusion. Under a leave-one-session-out protocol on two public datasets, TSMCA-Net achieves the highest mean accuracy across three cognitive paradigms (71.41% MI, 86.36% MA, 80.30% WG), outperforming all 12 baselines in absolute accuracy and achieving statistical significance in 31 of 36 pairwise comparisons (p<0.05). Perturbation experiments demonstrate 38%-62% smaller accuracy degradation under simulated spatial perturbations.

ai.summary: Proposed TSMCA-Net, a lightweight cross-session EEG-fNIRS decoder with <1M parameters and sub-8ms inference latency, using multi-view factorization and asymmetric cross-attention for role-aware fusion. Under leave-one-session-out on two public datasets, it achieved highest mean accuracy across three cognitive paradigms (71.41% MI, 86.36% MA, 80.30% WG), outperforming 12 baselines with statistical significance in 31 of 36 pairwise comparisons.

papers.title: Feature-Based Machine-Learning Spike Marking in Signal and Source Space EEG: A Proof-of-Principle Case Study of Focal Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Accurate detection of interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) in electroencephalography (EEG) plays a crucial role in epilepsy diagnosis. Our work investigates the classification of IEDs using Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) trained on EEG data represented in both signal and source space, in a proof-of-principle case study of focal epilepsy. Source waveforms were computed using a standard clinical source analysis procedure for the dipolar IED topographies, an equivalent current dipole model in a three-compartment head volume conductor model fitted using either a 1-parameter fixed-orientation or a 3-parameter projection approach, both localized to a single best-fit position during the rising flank of the IED. The ANN was trained on raw and feature-extracted versions of signal space and source space data. Feature extraction significantly improved performance across all domains. The highest accuracy (0.98) was achieved in signal space using Katz Fractional Dimension (KFD). In source space analyses, the 1-parameter and 3-parameter models achieved a maximum accuracy of 0.84, with statistical features performing best for the fixed-orientation model and KFD for the free orientation model. Additionally, annotations from three independent expert markers showed considerable variability, with ANN performance falling within the range of inter-expert agreement. While the findings of our proof-of-principle case study support the potential of feature-informed ANN tools to assist expert evaluation in clinical workflows, data from a single patient cannot capture inter-individual variability. Future work on a large, multi-patient cohort is needed to develop a population-generalizable detector.

ai.reason: Focuses on feature-based classification of epileptiform discharges, with interpretable features like Katz fractal dimension; methods may transfer to artifact/spike detection in animal sleep EEG.
ai.summary: Proof-of-principle case study trained artificial neural networks to classify interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) from EEG in signal and source space for focal epilepsy. Feature extraction improved performance; highest accuracy (0.98) was in signal space with Katz Fractional Dimension (KFD), while source space models reached 0.84; annotation variability among experts framed ANN performance within inter-expert agreement range.

papers.title: An Interpretable Framework for Identifying EEG Spectral Biomarkers of Pathological Brain Aging.
papers.abstract: Background: Normal aging involves gradual declines in brain function, whereas neurodegenerative disorders show accelerated deterioration. Electroencephalography (EEG) captures alterations in brain oscillatory activity, making it promising for detecting neurodegenerative disorders. However, existing approaches often emphasize classification performance over spectral biomarker identification, limiting clinical translation. Methods: We propose an EEG-based framework integrating explainable machine learning, analyses of inter-subject heterogeneity and temporal stability, and probabilistic modeling to identify reproducible spectral biomarkers of pathological brain aging. Two independent public EEG datasets comprising cognitively normal (CN) individuals and patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) were analyzed. Spectral features from canonical frequency bands were analyzed using SHAP to identify reproducible biomarkers in two datasets. The identified biomarker was subsequently characterized through inter-subject heterogeneity, temporal stability, and empirical distributions to assess disease-related alterations in oscillatory activity. Results: Several spectral features showed consistent disease-related associations across classification tasks. The θ/α ratio emerged as a representative biomarker, showing reduced temporal stability and broader empirical distributions in most neurodegenerative groups than in CN. Conclusions: Reduced temporal stability of reproducible EEG spectral biomarkers may represent an observable signature of disrupted oscillatory brain organization during pathological aging. The proposed framework characterizes a dimension of EEG spectral biomarkers that static summaries discard, offering an interpretable basis on which future longitudinal studies may build diagnostic and monitoring tools.

ai.summary: Proposed an interpretable EEG framework integrating explainable machine learning and probabilistic modeling to identify spectral biomarkers of pathological brain aging across two independent datasets including cognitively normal and Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and frontotemporal dementia patients. The theta/alpha ratio emerged as a representative biomarker showing reduced temporal stability and broader empirical distributions in most neurodegenerative groups compared to controls.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-based Alzheimer's disease detection using multi-scale information retention transform: a subject-level comparison of machine learning classifiers.
papers.abstract: This exploratory study evaluates Multi-Scale Information Retention Transform (MSIRT), a feature-fusion framework for electroencephalography (EEG)-based Alzheimer's disease (AD) classification. Ratios between differential entropies were removed, and all EEG amplitudes were converted to volts before feature extraction because the transform is not invariant to arbitrary physical units. Revised MSIRT combines fuzzy entropy (FE), permutation entropy (PE), and differential entropy (DE) using training-fold normalization and cross-feature products. The framework was evaluated on OpenNeuro ds004504 (29 healthy controls and 36 participants with AD) using participant-level cross-validation. With Random Forest (RF) held fixed, direct concatenation achieved 84.62% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.8956, whereas revised MSIRT achieved 86.15% accuracy and an AUC of 0.9004. An interaction-only control achieved 80.00% accuracy and an AUC of 0.8908. Because the no-product transform is feature-wise strictly monotonic, it was treated as an RF invariance control rather than a source of new predictive information. The paired AUC difference between revised MSIRT and concatenation was 0.0048 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, -0.0067 to 0.0192; paired permutation p = 0.3780). In 20 sex-balanced resamples, revised MSIRT had a mean AUC of 0.8846. These results do not establish statistical superiority or clinical utility.

ai.reason: Lightweight entropy-feature fusion with subject-level validation and unit-normalization discussion is transferable to vigilance staging, though the clinical AD focus is adjacent.
ai.summary: This exploratory study evaluates MSIRT, a feature-fusion framework combining fuzzy entropy, permutation entropy, and differential entropy for EEG-based Alzheimer's disease classification. On OpenNeuro ds004504, revised MSIRT achieved 86.15% accuracy and AUC 0.9004 with Random Forest, compared to 84.62% accuracy and AUC 0.8956 for direct concatenation; the paired AUC difference was not statistically significant (p=0.3780), and the results do not establish clinical utility.

papers.title: An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network Model for Classifying Positive Affective States from EEG Data Considering Sleep Condition.
papers.abstract: The recognition of affective states from EEG recordings considering the sleep condition can be an important supporting tool in therapy and in the treatment of psychological or psychiatric disorders. Since sleep deprivation changes EEG characteristics, a two-stage framework is developed for affective state classification. First, a classification between "Normal Sleep" (NS) and "Sleep-Deprived" (SD) is conducted using resting-state EEG data. The data are then fed into one of two newly proposed, lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize four affective states. In the first stage, CNN-BiLSTM achieves 95.96% accuracy under window-level splitting and 70.46% under subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, while in the second stage the proposed models achieve 93.40% (NS) and 90.95% (SD) under window-level splitting, and 38.98% (NS) and 38.97% (SD) under cross-validation. The lower subject-independent accuracies reflect the class imbalance and the clustering of scores near the class boundaries, which make cross-subject four-class generalization challenging. As existing studies mostly classify momentary emotions without addressing sleep conditions, direct comparison with prior work is difficult; we therefore benchmarked our framework against several established baseline models, including SqueezeNet, EEGNet, ShallowConvNet, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. This study suggests that considering physiological states can improve multi-class classification of affective states from time-varying neurophysiological signals such as EEG. The framework performs strongly under window-level evaluation, whereas its performance under the stricter subject-independent setting is more limited and should be interpreted accordingly. It can nonetheless contribute to more comprehensive research in affective neuroscience.

ai.reason: Lightweight CNN framework that explicitly classifies Normal vs Sleep-Deprived states and reports subject-independent validation; directly relevant to efficient sleep/state classification though aimed at affect.
ai.summary: Developed a two-stage framework that first classifies normal versus sleep-deprived rest EEG with a CNN-BiLSTM, then feeds data into lightweight CNNs to recognize four affective states. It achieved 95.96% normal/sleep-deprived accuracy under window-level splitting but only 70.46% under subject-independent cross-validation, with affective-state accuracies of 93.40% (normal sleep) and 90.95% (sleep-deprived) under window-level splitting and about 39% under subject-independent cross-validation.

papers.title: Abnormal resting-state EEG microstates correlate with objective sleep parameters in insomnia disorder.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a common sleep disorder, and Electroencephalogram (EEG) microstates, which mirror transient cerebral cortical functional activity, are linked to sleep disorder pathophysiology. The microstate characteristics in insomnia patients and correlations with objective sleep parameters remain to be further explored. This study enrolled 45 insomnia disorder (ID) patients and 48 healthy controls (HC), collecting awake resting-state EEG for microstate analysis; 27 ID and 13 H C participants additionally completed overnight polysomnography (PSG), and exploratory correlation analyses of microstate and PSG data performed for the ID group. Compared with HC, ID patients had markedly shorter duration of microstate A and B, higher occurrence and contribution of microstate C, and reduced duration, occurrence and contribution of microstate D (p < 0.05). ID patients also showed significantly lower transition probabilities of A→D, B→D, D→A and D→B (p < 0.01), and higher probabilities of A→C, B→C, C→A and C→B (p < 0.05). Correlation analyses revealed that in the ID, microstate D occurrence was negatively correlated with rapid eye movement sleep proportion (REM Sleep%, r = -0.427, p = 0.026) and positively correlated with non-rapid eye movement sleep stage 1 proportion (S1%, r = 0.385, p = 0.047). ID patients present significant abnormalities in EEG microstates, and the occurrence of microstate D is correlated with objective sleep indicators of PSG. These findings suggest that EEG microstate parameters may reflect abnormalities in the sleep architecture of ID and may provide references for analyzing the cortical hyperarousal mechanism of chronic insomnia, constructing objective assessment schemes, and developing targeted neuroregulation interventions.

ai.topic: EEG microstates and sleep in insomnia
ai.reason: Examines EEG microstates and their correlation with sleep parameters; relevant to sleep research and EEG analysis, though more clinical than computational.
ai.summary: This study compared resting-state EEG microstates in 45 insomnia disorder patients and 48 healthy controls, finding shorter microstate A and B duration, increased microstate C occurrence/contribution, and reduced microstate D metrics in patients. In the insomnia group, microstate D occurrence negatively correlated with REM sleep proportion and positively correlated with stage 1 sleep proportion, suggesting microstate parameters reflect altered sleep architecture.

papers.title: Topology-enhanced machine learning for speech signal processing.
papers.abstract: In artificial-intelligence-aided signal processing, existing deep learning models often exhibit a black-box structure. Here, conceptually beyond spectral analysis, we demonstrate that topological methods not only effectively capture intrinsic and complex structural information but can also enhance neural networks. We provide a transparent methodology, TopCap, to capture topological features inherent in time series for basic machine learning. Compared to prior approaches, we obtain descriptors that probe finer information such as the vibration of a time series. Notably, in classifying voiced and voiceless consonants, TopCap achieves an accuracy consistently standing in comparison with neural network models. Moreover, by integrating TopCap features into those neural networks, our approach improves upon state-of-the-art methods in terms of robustness against noise, as well as accuracy, stability, convergence of loss function, and interpretability.

ai.reason: Introduces topological feature extraction for time series that is interpretable and transferable to neural signals, potentially useful for EEG/EMG analysis.
ai.summary: The authors introduce TopCap, a transparent topological method for extracting structural features from time series that can enhance basic machine learning and neural network models. In classifying voiced and voiceless consonants, TopCap achieved accuracy comparable to neural networks, and when integrated into neural networks, it improved robustness to noise, accuracy, stability, loss convergence, and interpretability over state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: A GRAPH CONVOLUTION BASED DUAL-BRANCH NETWORK FOR DECODING OF UPPER-LIMB MOTOR IMAGERY EEG SIGNALS.
papers.abstract: Analysing motor imagery EEG signals using conventional Euclidean feature computation is challenging due to low spatial resolution, non-stationarity, and complex inter-channel dependencies, which limit robust subject-independent generalization in brain-computer interface systems. This study proposes a graph-based convolutional framework for subject-independent decoding of upper-limb motor imagery. The model integrates graph convolution with skip connections and handcrafted time-frequency features, together with parallel spatial and temporal convolutional pathways. Graph convolution captures functional connectivity between electrodes, while convolutional modules enhance spatial-temporal representation learning. Subject-independent evaluation is ensured using Stratified Group K-Fold (SGKF) and Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) validation protocols. The framework was evaluated on the PhysioNet, BCI IV-2a, and BCI IV-2b datasets using multiple electrode configurations. For the PhysioNet dataset, three upper-limb classes were considered, achieving SGKF accuracies of 86.42%, 91.01%, and 93.91% using 64, 21, and 5 electrodes, respectively, and LOSO accuracies of 92.25%, 95.72%, and 96.01%. On the BCI IV-2a dataset, SGKF accuracies of 86.13%, 89.01%, and 92.33% were obtained, with LOSO accuracies reaching 97.12% using five electrodes. For the BCI IV-2b dataset, accuracies of 88.60% (SGKF) and 93.35% (LOSO) were achieved using only three electrodes. The proposed graph-based framework demonstrates competitive performance to representative graph-based methods while requiring fewer trainable parameters and EEG electrodes. These findings demonstrate that graph-based deep learning enables accurate, subject-independent motor imagery decoding with reduced model complexity and minimal electrode usage, supporting practical and resource-efficient brain-computer interface systems.

papers.title: A Pilot Study of the Feasibility of In-Ear EEG for Long-Term Temporal Lobe Brain Wave Monitoring.
papers.abstract: Background: Traditional scalp electroencephalography (EEG), though clinically validated, presents significant limitations, including lengthy setup, patient discomfort, and limited mobility. These factors hinder its utility for long-term ambulatory monitoring. In-ear EEG offers a promising alternative by leveraging the ear canal's anatomical proximity to the temporal lobes and natural mechanical stability. To address this, we developed SeizEAR, a standardized, three-size in-ear EEG system using paste-based electrodes with cross-ear referencing. Methods: This pilot study evaluated SeizEAR devices featuring small, medium, and large earpieces with superior and inferior paste-based electrodes in each ear, configured in a cross-ear reference scheme. It included five healthy adults who underwent recording sessions of approximately three hours (2.4 to 3.3 h). Electrode impedance was monitored against the acquisition system's threshold indicator, with simultaneous scalp EEG from T7/T8 electrodes serving as the reference. Participants rated comfort on a 0-5 Likert scale every 30 min. Results: In-ear recordings showed moderate, band-dependent correspondence with ipsilateral temporal scalp electrodes, strongest in the delta and alpha bands and weakest in beta, and correspondence was consistently higher against a geometrically matched T7-T8 bipolar derivation than against a single referenced electrode. In-ear alpha reactivity to eye closure was present but attenuated relative to scalp. Comfort ratings remained high over the final two hours of wear, with no reported adverse events. Conclusions: SeizEAR acquired in-ear EEG that corresponded moderately with temporal scalp EEG and was well-tolerated over multi-hour wear in healthy adults. These preliminary findings support further development of a standardized in-ear EEG system and require confirmation in an adequately powered sample.

papers.title: Sleep EEG oscillations and synaptic plasticity in memory consolidation across NREM and REM sleep.
papers.abstract: Based on a synthesis of recent advances, this review elucidates the distinct yet synergistic roles of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep in memory consolidation. During NREM sleep, cortical slow oscillations (SOs) establish a temporal framework by alternating between UP and DOWN states, facilitating cross-regional communication. SOs phase-couple with thalamic spindles to coordinate hippocampal sharp-wave ripples (SWRs), thereby driving the reactivation and transfer of labile hippocampal memories to neocortical networks for long-term storage. Concurrent synaptic homeostasis optimises network efficiency through global downscaling while selectively strengthening memory-relevant connections. In REM sleep, theta oscillations synchronise limbic-prefrontal-hippocampal circuits, and ponto-geniculo-occipital (PGO) waves further integrate emotional and procedural memories. The cholinergically dominant, monoamine-depleted neurochemical milieu of REM sleep promotes dendritic spine remodelling and sparse neuronal reactivation, enabling affective decoupling and synaptic refinement. Despite progress, key challenges remain in understanding cross-frequency oscillatory coupling among slow oscillations, spindles, ripples and REM-specific rhythms, glial contributions and clinical translation. Future integration of high-density electrophysiology with computational approaches may yield mechanistic models and clinically relevant biomarkers for sleep-based cognitive monitoring and intervention.

papers.title: CSTO-Net: Cross-View Spectral-Transport and Topology-Operator Network for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.abstract: Multi-view electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition must decide how the spectral graph sets of different connectivity views correspond and how their graph propagation operators interact. We present CSTO-Net, a cross-view spectral-transport and topology-operator network for EEG-based emotion recognition.Approach: CSTO-Net integrates three window-wise views: dynamic differential entropy (DDE) as node attributes, amplitude-envelope Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) graphs, and phase-locking value (PLV) graphs. Cross-View Spectral Transport Routing (CSTR) formulates PCC-PLV spectral correspondence as an entropy-regularized optimal-transport problem with explicit marginal constraints, deliberately separating correspondence estimation from band-importance estimation. Directional Cross-Topology Modulation (DCTM) performs ordered composition of the two routed propagation operators on shared node features and encodes order-dependent propagation discrepancy via a provably skew-symmetric graph-operator commutator with signed decomposition.Main results: On the Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals (DEAP) dataset, CSTO-Net achieves 93.95 ± 2.50% valence and 94.97 ± 2.72% arousal accuracy under the subject-dependent setting, and 93.73% and 94.54% under participant-wise five-fold subject-independent cross-validation across 32 participants. On the SJTU Emotion EEG Dataset (SEED), it achieves 93.12% under the standard subject-dependent split, 91.36% under 15-fold leave-one-subject-out evaluation across 15 participants, and 98.05 ± 2.32% under subject-dependent five-fold cross-validation. Ablation studies confirm that both CSTR and DCTM contribute substantially to recognition accuracy.Significance: These results demonstrate that explicit cross-view spectral correspondence and topology-operator-level interaction provide complementary benefits for EEG emotion recognition, offering an interpretable route for modeling order-sensitive interactions between functional connectivity views.

papers.title: Fear-EEG-AI: A Conceptual and Operational Framework for Designing EEG-AI Systems for the Inference of Fear-Compatible Neurophysiological States.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and artificial intelligence (AI) are central tools in affective computing, yet fear-related inference remains constrained by a gap between experimental performance and deployable evidence: high accuracy on controlled datasets guarantees neither neurobiological specificity, nor robustness across users, nor traceable inference. EEG does not measure fear directly; it captures cortical dynamics compatible with threat processing, arousal or vigilance. This paper introduces the Fear-EEG-AIFramework, a technology-independent architecture for designing, validating and deploying EEG-AI systems targeting fear-compatible neurophysiological states. Building on a prior systematic review, it organizes development into three hierarchical levels-neurobiological foundation, neuroelectric correlates and computational modeling-governed by six cross-cutting principles, and makes them evaluable through eight observable dimensions, the Fear-EEG-AI Alignment Index (FAI) and five validation evidence levels. Applied to the eight eligible studies of that corpus by two raters who had not drafted the instrument, with adjudication by a third, the rubric reached 67.2% exact agreement (quadratic-weighted κ=0.741; ICC(2,1) =0.744). Under 10,000 admissible weightings the equal-weight ordering survived in 10.1% of draws, and one of 56 ordered pairs met a stability criterion fixed before the pairwise results were tabulated. The index is therefore reported as a descriptor of methodological documentation and not as a ranking of implementations.

papers.title: Balancing Local and Global Dependencies in EEG Emotion Recognition via Multi-Scale Hybrid Attention.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition remains challenging due to the low signal-to-noise ratio, non-stationarity, strong inter-subject variability, and the distribution of affect-related information across multiple temporal resolutions. Although recent deep architectures have increasingly combined multi-scale local feature extraction with global dependency modeling, the adaptive integration of multi-scale representations before global encoding remains comparatively underexplored. To address this issue, we propose DSFConformer, an EEG emotion-recognition framework integrating multi-scale spatiotemporal convolution, Dynamic Sparse Feature Fusion (DSFF), and lightweight Transformer-based global modeling. The multi-scale encoder captures complementary local EEG dynamics at different temporal resolutions, while DSFF performs sample-adaptive feature reweighting and sparse suppression to reduce the influence of redundant or noise-sensitive responses. A Lite Transformer is subsequently employed to model global contextual dependencies with reduced computational cost. Experiments on the SEED dataset were conducted under complementary evaluation protocols. DSFConformer achieved an accuracy of 96.08% under chronological block-wise segment-level cross-validation. Under the stricter trial-wise protocol, it achieved 78.81% accuracy, statistically comparable to EEG-Conformer at 78.77%, with no significant paired difference. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that multi-scale convolution and DSFF provide the primary recognition-performance gains, whereas the Lite Transformer mainly improves computational efficiency while preserving comparable accuracy. Cross-session and leave-one-subject-out analyses further assess model robustness and generalization. Overall, the results indicate that adaptive sparse fusion of multi-scale EEG representations provides an effective approach for balancing local representation learning, noise-aware feature integration, and efficient global dependency modeling.

papers.title: Auditory paradigm-dependent EEG feature screening and representation for distinguishing consciousness states in male patients with disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Accurate assessment of disorders of consciousness (DoC), including minimally conscious state (MCS) and unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS/VS), remains a major challenge in clinical neurorehabilitation. EEG-based biomarkers offer a non-invasive approach for characterizing residual brain activity, yet their discriminative sensitivity may depend on auditory stimulus design. EEG recordings were obtained from 15 male patients with DoC during four auditory stimulation paradigms. Nonlinear, spectral power, and graph-theoretic features were extracted, yielding 136 candidate features. All individual features were independently evaluated using patient-level leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) to characterize paradigm- and feature-domain-specific predictive performance. In a complementary exploratory optimization analysis, univariate statistical screening identified 26 features with nominal group differences (p < 0.05); these features were subsequently subjected to within-fold K-means clustering and principal component analysis (PCA), and compared with directly combined feature representations for MCS versus UWS/VS classification and CRS-R score regression. In the single-feature benchmark, the reversed-word sequence paradigm showed relatively higher averaged classification performance, while nonlinear features demonstrated comparatively stronger classification characteristics than spectral power and graph-theoretic features. In the optimization analysis, the PCA-derived representation achieved competitive classification performance, whereas the direct combination of all statistically screened features achieved the highest observed classification accuracy. Regression performance was generally limited. These findings suggest that auditory stimulus design and EEG feature representation may influence the discrimination of consciousness states in DoC. In this small-sample exploratory study, reversed-word auditory stimulation and nonlinear EEG features showed promising discriminative characteristics, while direct feature combination provided additional predictive information for categorical classification. Further validation in larger and independent cohorts is required.

papers.title: A jointly optimized hybrid framework for epileptic EEG artifact classification.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of artifacts in long-term electroencephalography (EEG) recordings is essential for reliable automated epilepsy analysis, as artifacts may obscure epileptiform patterns and degrade downstream detection performance. However, existing methods still face challenges in complementary feature integration and coordinated optimization of feature selection and classifier parameters. To address the limited feature representation capability of handcrafted methods and the limited interpretability of deep learning approaches, this paper proposes a hybrid EEG artifact classification framework that integrates complementary feature representation with the joint optimization of feature selector and classifier parameters. Specifically, handcrafted temporal-spectral-entropy features are fused with deep features extracted by a lightweight ResNet-LSTM network. A novel Class Neighborhood Discrimination (CND) method is employed for discriminative feature selection, while an Adaptive Seagull Optimization Algorithm (ASOA) jointly optimizes the parameters of the CND feature selector and the Random Forest (RF) classifier within a unified optimization framework. Experimental results on the Temple University Artifact Corpus (TUAR) and clinical EEG recordings show that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 99.30% on the originally constructed dataset and maintains 98.15% accuracy on an additional recording-independent clinical test set. The proposed method also shows consistent performance across multiple evaluation metrics, including MCC, Kappa, and GDR, and outperforms representative feature selection methods, optimization strategies, and classifiers. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively combines interpretability, discriminative feature representation, and joint optimization, providing an accurate and robust solution for epileptic EEG artifact classification.

papers.title: EEG-ECG/HRV associations under multi-stage cognitive stress: characterization and mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Mental stress affects cognitive, emotional, and cardiovascular function, but subjective stress scales are susceptible to individual bias. Brain-heart coupling offers a potential approach to stress assessment. This study examined stage-dependent EEG-ECG/HRV associations during mental arithmetic and Stroop tasks. Sixty healthy adults were recruited, EEG and ECG were recorded during baseline rest, four mental-arithmetic stages, inter-task rest, and four Stroop stages. Stage-specific Spearman correlations characterized between-participant associations between five EEG band-power measures and seven ECG/HRV indices. Mixed-effects models separating within- and between-participant effects tested whether within-participant associations varied across difficulty stages and tasks. Significant EEG-HRV correlations decreased in number after task onset and partially recovered during inter-task rest. Mental arithmetic showed more pronounced negative high-frequency EEG-vagal HRV correlations, whereas Stroop showed Theta/Beta-HR associations at onset and sustained Alpha-RMSSD associations during middle-to-late stages. Neither task showed FDR-significant stage-averaged within-participant associations. Within-participant EEG × difficulty-stage interactions were FDR-significant for 12 of 35 whole-frontal associations during mental arithmetic and none during Stroop. Combined models identified five significant within-participant EEG × difficulty × task interactions. No linear difficulty interactions survived FDR correction in sensitivity analyses. These findings support stage-dependent EEG-ECG/HRV associations in this fixed-order cognitive-stress paradigm. They may inform physiologically interpretable candidate measures for objective mental stress assessment and wearable monitoring.

papers.title: Decoding user satisfaction during reading of pre-defined question-answer pairs: BCI approach using delta and gamma EEG.
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs) has intensified the need for robust evaluation frameworks to align artificial intelligence (AI) behavior with human expectations. While current reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) strategies heavily rely on explicit, post-hoc self-reports, these metrics are fundamentally limited by subjective biases and user non-compliance. To address this, the current study presents a novel brain-computer interface (BCI) framework that systematically characterizes the continuous, implicit neural correlates of user satisfaction and dissatisfaction during a reading-based evaluative task involving pre-validated LLM-generated question-answer pairs. Sixty-four-channel electroencephalography (EEG) data were recorded from 30 participants while they read and evaluated various LLM-generated responses. To capture genuine subjective experiences, individual trials were relabeled based on post-trial 5-point Likert scale ratings into five distinct evaluative states, and spatiotemporal spectral analyses were performed. A ShallowFBCSPNet architecture was further used to evaluate single-trial classification between the very satisfied and very dissatisfied conditions under a subject-mixed cross-validation scheme. Spatiotemporal spectral analyses revealed distinct neural oscillatory dynamics that temporally dissociate satisfaction and dissatisfaction. When reading highly satisfactory responses, a pronounced, sustained enhancement of low-frequency delta power was observed within the bilateral frontotemporal areas during the middle (4-8 s) and late (8-12 s) reading intervals, indexing high-order cognitive consolidation and reward processing. Conversely, processing highly dissatisfactory responses led to a localized suppression of high-frequency gamma power in the right frontotemporal region during the early interval (0-4 s), reflecting an immediate affective appraisal and expectation violation. Utilizing the ShallowFBCSPNet architecture, the system successfully discriminated between the "very satisfied" and "very dissatisfied" states, achieving an average accuracy of 81% under a subject-mixed cross-validation scheme. These findings demonstrate that user evaluative states are encoded via distinct frequency-specific cortical networks over differing temporal windows. By bridging cognitive neuroscience and artificial intelligence, this study establishes the conceptual and empirical foundation for passive BCI-driven implicit feedback channels, laying groundwork toward future real-time paradigms for next-generation LLM alignment; the classification result should be interpreted as a feasibility demonstration rather than an estimate of real-world decoding accuracy.

papers.title: Individualized TMS-EEG mapping reveals clinically relevant early prefrontal cortical activity in major depressive disorder.
papers.abstract: To determine whether individualized TMS-EEG mapping improves assessment of early cortical responses in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) compared with conventional Beam F3 targeting and their association with depressive symptom severity. Single-pulse TMS-EEG was performed in 30 patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and 15 healthy controls. Individualized mapping identified DLPFC stimulation sites and intensities that minimized artifacts while eliciting robust early TMS-evoked potentials (>6 μV within 60 ms). Responses were compared with Beam F3 stimulation at 120% resting motor threshold. Early cortical activity was quantified using global mean field power (GMFP) and region-of-interest (ROI) area-under-the-curve (AUC) during the 10-30 ms post-stimulation interval. Individualized mapping produced distinct early cortical responses and significantly smaller early GMFP and ROI AUC responses (q < 0.001) compared to Beam F3 stimulation. Within the MDD group, lower GMFP AUC was associated with greater depression (PHQ-9: ρ = - 0.43, q = 0.046) and anxiety severity (GAD-7: ρ = - 0.58, q = 0.008). Lower ROI AUC was associated with greater depressive symptoms (PHQ-9: ρ = - 0.57, q = 0.008; QIDS-SR: ρ = - 0.48, q = 0.033) and anxiety severity (GAD-7: ρ = - 0.45, q = 0.040). No significant clinical associations were observed for Beam F3-derived measures. Individualized TMS-EEG mapping identifies clinically relevant early DLPFC responses not detected using conventional Beam F3 targeting. Individualized targeting improves the sensitivity of prefrontal TMS-EEG and may enhance detection of early cortical responses associated with depressive and anxiety severity.

papers.title: Neurovascular coupling in simultaneous EEG-fNIRS studies: A scoping review of analytical frameworks and clinical applications.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) have been used across cognitive and physiological states and in diverse clinical populations. However, the interpretation of cross-modal coupling remains difficult because findings from different analytical frameworks, populations, and experimental conditions have not been systematically mapped. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, and IEEE Xplore were searched through February 10, 2026, for studies that quantitatively related simultaneously recorded EEG and fNIRS signals. Two reviewers independently screened the records. Findings were synthesized narratively, and analytical pipelines were mapped across the signal domain, feature extraction, coupling metric, and temporal lag handling. Fifty-seven studies were included. Amplitude-based studies related event-related potentials and oscillatory EEG features to focal hemodynamic responses, with associations varying across electrophysiological features, cortical regions, and task conditions. Frequency- and scale-specific analyses identified band-dependent relationships, while coupling at ultra-slow scales showed sensitivity to vascular and systemic physiological influences. Studies that explicitly modeled timing identified several-second offsets in some paradigms, while directional estimates varied across tasks and recording states. Network analyses showed partial and context-dependent correspondence between EEG- and fNIRS-derived measures, while model-based approaches characterized multivariate and predictive cross-modal relationships. Across frameworks, observed coupling differed with recording state, frequency band, cortical region, and temporal lag handling rather than representing a single quantity. Clinical findings were heterogeneous, and most condition-specific patterns were supported by small and methodologically diverse evidence bases. These findings support framework-matched analysis and pipeline-explicit reporting when interpreting EEG-fNIRS coupling.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
papers.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. This systematic review rigorously evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and methodological robustness of AI-generated EEG biomarkers by implementing the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST+AI). Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total N = 6,584). Methodological quality and validation strategies were assessed using the 34 signaling questions of the PROBAST+AI framework. The aggregate mean diagnostic accuracy across the literature was 93.38%, with deep learning architectures demonstrating superior metrics relative to classical machine learning (96.83% vs. 87.68%). Critically, external validation was restricted to 4.7% of the included studies. A pronounced performance discrepancy was observed between subject-wise (88.22%) and segment-wise (98.14%) validation protocols, indicating pervasive data leakage. Overall, 76.7% of the analyzed studies were characterized by a high risk of bias, predominantly stemming from suboptimal data partitioning and inadequate independent verification. Contemporary diagnostic accuracies appear to be artifactually elevated due to structural methodological deficiencies and data leakage. Consequently, current evidence does not support the immediate clinical implementation of AI-EEG biomarkers in schizophrenia. To facilitate translational progress, we propose a standardized methodological framework optimizing validation strategies.

papers.title: Neuroelectrophysiological correlates of extended cessation of consciousness in advanced meditators: A multimodal EEG and MEG study
papers.abstract: In some contemplative traditions, 'extended cessation' (EC) refers to a state of advanced meditation in which the meditator self-reports intentionally suppressing their own consciousness and re-emerging with a profound sense of clarity and equanimity. Here, we present the first electrophysiological study of EC, in which five meditators underwent concurrent electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) recording. EC significantly increased high-frequency global coherence in all five of the participants, yet it did not consistently affect Lempel-Ziv complexity or power across participants. Our results provide preliminary evidence that the neural signatures of EC may be distinct from other states that are characterized by a loss of consciousness, including deep sleep and anesthesia. EC may not be simply 'switching off' consciousness but rather reorganizing the neural dynamics that underlie consciousness.

papers.title: Video EEG in pediatric epilepsy: Diagnostic significance and association between frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to compare video electroencephalogram (VEEG) and routine electroencephalogram (EEG) in childhood epilepsy diagnosis and analyze the correlation between EEG frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity. One hundred and sixty children suspected of having epilepsy underwent routine EEG and VEEG examinations. Diagnostic efficacy and detection rates were compared. Cognitive function was evaluated in 80 children diagnosed with epilepsy, who were allocated into normal intelligence (35 cases), borderline intelligence (25 cases), and intelligence-impaired (20 cases) groups. Clinical data, EEG parameters, and their correlation with cognitive impairment were analyzed. VEEG showed higher sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value, and detection rates of epileptiform discharges, synchronous clinical seizures, and clinical symptoms than routine EEG (p < 0.05). Clinical characteristics and EEG parameters differed among the three groups (p < 0.05). The relative power of δ and θ bands and the awake and sleep discharge indices were positively correlated with cognitive impairment severity (r = 0.300, 0.643, 0.622, and 0.456), whereas α and β band power were negatively correlated (r = -0.515 and -0.410) (all p < 0.001). VEEG demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than routine EEG, and EEG frequency band power was correlated with cognitive impairment severity.

papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.abstract: How do leader and follower roles shape the brain mechanisms that support coordinated action between people? This question has therapeutic relevance for conditions such as schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder, where the capacity for reciprocal social coordination is a defining vulnerability. Here, we propose a tetradic framework and examine sensorimotor coordination in 16 healthy adult pairs (15 included in EEG analyses) using dual-brain EEG hyperscanning and a 2x2 within-subject design crossing Role (Leader/Follower) and Condition (Mirroring/Matching). Mirroring required resonance with a partner's movement; Matching required its controlled transformation. This contrast was designed to dissociate automatic from controlled coordination. Behaviourally, Mirroring produced a robust Follower reaction-time advantage: pooling an independent behavioural-only cohort (combined N=64) revealed a smaller Leader advantage, consistent with role-dependent attention-inhibition gating. At the neural level, tonic power and significant phasic condition clusters were greater during Matching than Mirroring, while role-dependent phasic clusters suggested an anticipatory sequence around Leader responses and post-response gating and rebound around Follower responses. Information-theoretic decomposition identified Leader-weighted predictive information in frontal and posterior perceptual regions, Follower-specific adaptive information across frontoparietal and sensorimotor cortices, sparse Synergy in lateral occipital, fusiform, and paracentral cortices, and Redundancy linking pars opercularis and lateral occipital cortex. These findings characterize tetradic coordination within dyads as a multiscale, role-asymmetric architecture in which top-down predictive control and bottom-up adaptive regulation are functionally dissociable. The tetradic framework provides an organizing scaffold for this dissociation, and the role-specific signatures it reveals may offer candidate biomarkers for clinical populations in whom interpersonal coordination is disrupted.

papers.title: Multimodal Machine Learning Approaches to Detect Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Using Physiological and Behavioural Biomarkers: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Background: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by persistent symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity that can affect individuals throughout childhood and adulthood. Accurate and timely detection is important for appropriate support and management, but current assessment relies heavily on behavioural observations, clinical assessments, and information from multiple sources, which can be time-consuming and may be influenced by subjective judgement. These challenges have increased interest in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches that can analyse multiple physiological and behavioural data sources. Multimodal AI approaches may provide a more comprehensive and objective way to detect ADHD by combining complementary information from different data types. Objectives: This systematic review aimed to examine the use of ML and DL methods for ADHD detection using multimodal physiological and behavioural biomarkers, with particular attention to data sources, modelling approaches, multimodal fusion strategies, and reported diagnostic performance. Methods: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines to identify studies published from 2015 to 2026 that applied machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) methods to multimodal data for ADHD detection. We selected studies using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria and extracted and synthesised data from eligible studies. The review included 25 studies. The multimodal data sources examined included neuroimaging modalities, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); physiological signals, including electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV), and electrodermal activity (EDA); behavioural assessments; and wearable or Internet of Things (IoT)-based measures. We also assessed the included studies for methodological quality and model performance to identify current evidence, limitations, and future research needs. Results: The included studies varied substantially in design and sample size, with participant numbers ranging from 22 to 15,883. Most studies used cross-sectional designs. Early multimodal fusion approaches frequently reported diagnostic accuracies above 80%, demonstrating the potential value of combining complementary physiological and behavioural information. Reported informative biomarkers included frontal brain activity, heart rate patterns, and oculomotor behaviour. However, substantial differences in data sources, acquisition procedures, feature extraction, modelling techniques, and evaluation protocols limited direct comparison across studies. Small sample sizes and a lack of standardised data collection and methodological protocols also challenged the generalisability and reliability of the reported findings. Conclusions: Multimodal machine learning and deep learning approaches show considerable potential for improving ADHD detection by integrating complementary physiological and behavioural information. However, substantial heterogeneity in data collection, devices, datasets, validation procedures, and reporting limits comparability and generalisability across studies. Future research should prioritise standardised data-collection protocols, larger and more diverse datasets (including children, adolescents, and participants from different cultural backgrounds), leakage-safe validation, and independent multi-site testing. Fusion strategies should be selected based on modality compatibility and study objectives. Improving model interpretability alongside predictive performance will also support clinical trust and real-world adoption.

papers.title: Case Report: Right frontal periventricular heterotopia underlying secondary network epilepsy with a Lennox-Gastaut phenotype: multimodal SEEG, CCEP, and rs-fMRI evidence.
papers.abstract: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) is generally regarded as a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy involving distributed brain networks, although a focal structural abnormality may occasionally recruit bilateral cortical and thalamic circuits and produce an LGS phenotype. We characterized the spatiotemporal organization of such a network and its changes after focal SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC). A 50-year-old woman with drug-resistant epilepsy, multiple seizure types, diffuse slow spike-and-wave discharges, generalized paroxysmal fast activity, intellectual impairment, and right frontal periventricular heterotopia (PVH) underwent stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG). Cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) were acquired before and after SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC). Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI), obtained before and 3 months after RF-TC, was analyzed using three seeds: the entire right frontal PVH and the right and left centromedian thalamic nuclei (CM). SEEG identified the earliest sustained ictal activity within the sampled right frontal PVH-related medial contacts, accompanied by high-frequency activity. This was followed by ipsilateral lateral frontal recruitment, contralateral frontal synchronization, and subsequent bilateral CM involvement. Two-stage RF-TC of the onset and early-recruited networks was followed by seizure freedom through 9 months. After RF-TC, right-sided stimulation produced markedly attenuated lesion-related CCEP responses, whereas left-sided responses and responses between thalamic contacts showed little appreciable change. Descriptive rs-fMRI difference maps demonstrated decreased local frontal connectivity around the treated territory and increased long-range connectivity for the PVH seed; both CM seeds showed predominantly increased connectivity with distributed cortical and cerebellar regions. In this patient, a focal PVH-related epileptogenic network was associated with secondary bilateral cortical and thalamic recruitment underlying an LGS phenotype. CCEP and rs-fMRI captured complementary aspects of postoperative network change: attenuation of stimulation-evoked propagation and postoperative changes in intrinsic functional connectivity, respectively.

papers.title: Investigation of human defence responses in a virtual reality environment: an EEG study.
papers.abstract: A predatory imminence continuum displays the perceived imminence of threat to visualise the risk to the prey. Most human studies have utilised static paradigms that may lack ecological validity and limit the exploration of defensive behaviours. Therefore, the present study investigates Fight/ Flight defence responses and underlying neural correlates using EEG under varying conditions of threat proximity and escape availability using a virtual reality (VR) environment. The experiment consisted of a desktop VR environment, including training and experimental phases (5 conditions). Conditions 1 to 4, except 5, included a threat avatar. The conditions differed based on threat proximity (distal/ proximal) and participant's escapability (escape/no-escape). Twenty trials were presented, with each condition presented 4 times. Participants responded with a Fight/Flight response to the threat, followed by a 10-s rest scene and a 5-s fixation. A significant difference in reaction time was observed, indicating distinction based on threat proximity and escapability. A heightened Fight response was observed across all conditions. This pattern may reflect the absence of consequences associated with defensive actions compared to real-life scenarios. For the electrophysiological analysis, ERP analysis indicated a significant difference in the Late frontal activity at the F1 electrode across all conditions. This may suggest tentative cognitive processing during the period surrounding defensive response (Fight or Flight) selection and execution. Together, the findings indicate that although the lack of consequences may have promoted the Fight response more in the VR scenarios, the neural responses may have shown differences in cognitive processing.

papers.title: Does delayed removal of stereo-EEG electrodes following radiofrequency thermocoagulation increase haemorrhage?
papers.abstract: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC) is used in the assessment and treatment of medically refractory epilepsy, typically with electrode removal immediately following ablation. Our SEEG-guided RF-TC protocol includes the option of three further days of recording following thermocoagulation, prior to electrode removal. It is not known whether delayed removal of electrodes following RF-TC may increase the risk of haemorrhage. To compare the rate and volume of intracranial haemorrhage with immediate versus delayed electrode removal following RF-TC. 217 SEEG electrodes from 16 consecutive patients were retrospectively reviewed for haemorrhage. 3D T1-weighted (T1w) and Susceptibility Weighted (SWI) imaging were reviewed for haemorrhage along the electrode tract and at the site of RF-TC. The primary outcome measure was the per-electrode volume of T1w detectable haemorrhage at the site of RF-TC in electrodes removed immediately after RF-TC, compared to electrodes removed 3-days after RF-TC. Secondary outcomes compared the incidence and volume of T1w haemorrhage along the electrode tract in thermocoagulated versus non-thermocoagulated electrodes, presumed due to reflect haemorrhage from electrode insertion/removal. We also describe the temporal evolution of the MRI appearance of haemorrhage following SEEG-guided RF-TC. No clinically significant haemorrhages occurred. At the site of RF-TC a small amount of blood product is universally present but there was no significant difference in per-electrode haemorrhage volume following delayed (93.8 ± 39.8 mm3; ~diameter 5.6 mm) and immediate (80.0 ± 37.5 mm3; ~ diameter 5.3 mm) removal of electrodes (Mann-Whitney U test, p = 0.10). At the cortical surface there was no significant difference in the rate of T1w haemorrhage between thermocoagulated and non-thermocoagulated electrodes (63.1% vs 52.5%, p = 0.12, chi-squared). Delayed removal of electrodes post-RF-TC allows assessment of response to RFA and the opportunity for further thermocoagulation if necessary. This exploratory study found no significant increase in haemorrhage volume with delayed electrode removal following RF-TC but a larger study would be required to definitively estimate haemorrhage risk.
